messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: make/local magic incantation?
parts:
I keep getting bitten by my make/local going away, which causes
all testing to revert to super-slow g++ -O3 mode rather than
the clang++ -O0 I want.

How should I be managing my make/local so that it doesn't go away
every time I change branches?

And could someone remind me what's supposed to be in it because
I appear to have wiped mine with git somehow (maybe one of those
getting rid of everything not in git commands or something?).

- Bob

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] make/local magic incantation?
parts:
If the file is in your .gitignore or more appropriately in your
.git/info/exclude (e.g. so only for your local repo only), then it
won't be wiped out when changing branches. The latter won't wipe it
out even if it's not .gitignore'd in the new branch. (If it's in
.gitignore on both branches it should not be wiped out.)

Another option is to use smudge/clean filters locally and a
.gitattributes filter for make/local. That's a more correct but more
complicated option.

Yet another option is to "git stash save -u" before switching
branches, then "git stash pop" after, but that could have unintended
side effects.

Ido

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] make/local magic incantation?
parts:
Did you do a git clean -d -f -f -x? That'd get rid of any
ignored/untracked files as well as any local changes. Just be careful
with git clean, especially with all those extra parameters.

Alternatively, change the build system to use something like
$HOME/.config/stan/make.local or similar out-of-tree path (and make it
YELL LOUDLY that it is doing so)...that might be a better option.
